'''Edmund Frederick Robertson''' (born 1 June 1943) is a British mathematician who is a [[professor emeritus]] of [[pure mathematics]] at the [[University of St Andrews]].<ref name="cv" />

==Work==
Robertson is one of the creators of the [[MacTutor History of Mathematics archive]], along with John J. O'Connor. Robertson has written more than 100 research articles, mainly on the theory of [[group (mathematics)|groups]] and [[semigroups]]. He is also the author or co-author of 17 textbooks.<ref name=cv/>

Robertson obtained a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree at the [[University of St Andrews]] in 1965. He then went to the [[University of Warwick]], where he received a [[Master of Science]] degree in 1966 and a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree in 1968.<ref name="cv">{{Cite web|title=www-groups.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/~edmund/CV.html|url=http://www-groups.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/~edmund/CV.html|url-status=live|access-date=2020-09-06|website=www-groups.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210414231139/http://www-groups.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/~edmund/CV.html |archive-date=14 April 2021 }}</ref>

In 1998, he was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh]].<ref>[http://www.royalsoced.org.uk/fellowship/fellows.pdf ''Current Fellows''.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040627152829/http://www.royalsoced.org.uk/fellowship/fellows.pdf |date=27 June 2004}}  [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]]. Accessed 8 November 2008.</ref>

In 2015, he received together with his colleague O'Connor, the [[Hirst Prize and Lectureship|Hirst Prize]] of the [[London Mathematical Society]] for his work on the MacTutor History of Mathematics archive.<ref>[[Colm Mulcahy]]: [http://aperiodical.com/2015/07/mactutor-history-of-mathematics-website-creators-honoured-by-lms/ "MacTutor History of Mathematics website creators honoured by LMS"]. ''The Aperiodical'', 19 July 2015.</ref> His thesis on "Classes of Generalised Nilpotent Groups" was done with Stewart E. Stonehewer.<ref>[https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=46708&fChrono=1 Edmund Frederick Robertson] Math Genealogy Project.</ref>

==Personal life==
He is with his wife, Helena, and his two sons.<ref>{{cite web|title=Edmund Robertson's Personal Home Page|url=http://turnbull.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/~edmund/|url-status=live|access-date=24 July 2021|website=turnbull.mcs.st-and.ac.uk|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020109234825/http://turnbull.mcs.st-and.ac.uk:80/~edmund/ |archive-date=9 January 2002 }}</ref>
